cards.b: Fixed: do not change with output in the short run (rent, insurance). Variable: change directly with output (materials, packaging).
Total cost = fixed costs + total variable costs. Total variable cost = variable cost per unit × output.
Total cost ÷ output. It falls as output rises because fixed costs are spread over more units.
Profit = total revenue − total costs. Total revenue = selling price × quantity sold.
Factors that reduce average cost as a business grows (e.g. bulk buying discounts).

cards.f: Five types of economy of scale

cards.b: Buying in bulk gives supplier discounts, lowering the cost per unit.
A large firm can afford advanced machinery and flow production, raising productivity.
Average costs rise when a business grows too large: poor communication, low employee commitment, weak coordination.
Selling price − variable cost per unit.
Fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit. Round UP to the next whole unit.
Actual (or planned) output − break-even output. Shows how far sales can fall before a loss.

cards.f: Break-even chart: where do lines start?
cards.b: Total cost line starts at the fixed-cost value on the y-axis; total revenue starts at the origin (0,0). They cross at break-even.

cards.f: Effect on break-even of a higher price
cards.b: Break-even output falls because contribution per unit rises. But sales may fall too, especially if demand is elastic.
Assumes all output is sold, constant price, costs are linear and fixed costs stay fixed; ignores competitors and other factors.

short.q: A business has fixed costs of €6,000, sells at €10 per unit and has variable costs of €4 per unit. Calculate the break-even output. [2]
The same business sells 1,400 units. Calculate the margin of safety and the profit. [3]
Explain what happens to break-even output if variable cost per unit rises. [3]
short.model: Contribution per unit falls, so more units must be sold to cover the fixed costs. Break-even output rises.
points: more units needed to cover fixed costs

short.q: Explain one economy of scale and one diseconomy of scale. [4]
short.model: Economy: bulk buying gives discounts so average cost falls. Diseconomy: in a very large firm, communication is slow so mistakes rise and average costs increase.

short.q: Explain two limitations of break-even analysis. [4]
short.model: It assumes all output is sold at one price, but discounts may be given. It also assumes costs stay constant, but material prices may change.
points: assumes all output is sold/constant price
